title: InterventionEvent
description: One line of data/interventions.jsonl: a deliberate, non-routine change to data/ or state.json made by a person or an agent (a repair, a reset, a hand edit). Routine collector runs are NOT interventions; they are run records. The point is that the next agent can see what was done, why, by whom, how to undo it, and whether it is finished. Append-only.

id.description: Same shape as run ids with an int- prefix.

verb.description: The repair verb or plan name, e.g. repair.regenerate-deletion, repair.rewalk-ids, repair.reset-source, repair.rewrite-records, manual.

target.description: What was touched: ts_ids, trumpstruth ids, state keys, files.

reason.description: One to three sentences. Link the lesson, decision, backlog item, or anomaly that motivated it.

plan.description: Path to the plan file the dry-run produced (e.g. output/plans/<id>.json) or 'inline'.

before.description: Summary of the state before: counts, check results, git commit.

after.description: Summary after: counts, check results, git commit.

undo.description: How to reverse it: usually 'git revert <sha>' plus any state.json key to restore.

links.description: Lesson ids, decision ids, backlog ids, commit shas.
